description: Cases for the Evidence rule added to SKILL.md (not part of upstream marketingskills). Same shape as evals.json plus `category` and a machine-checkable `check` block graded by tests/test_copy_editing_evidence_rule.py. These read a response; they do not run a model. Where an upstream eval or checklist item asks for a guarantee, proof or figure, the rule's precedence clause applies: a missing fact is met by a [NEED: ...] marker or a question to the business owner.

check_keys.forbid_need_for: regexes that must not match inside any [NEED: ...] marker (the fact was supplied, so asking for it again is wrong)
check_keys.strict_figures: outside [NEED: ...] spans, no dollar amount, percentage, number-with-unit or numeral of two or more digits that is absent from the prompt
check_keys.forbid: regexes that must not match outside [NEED: ...] spans
check_keys.require_any: at least one regex must match (owner-approval flag)

evals.prompt: Sharpen only this subhead. Product-marketing context file: 'Ledgerly drafts an invoice the day a project milestone closes. Median time to payment is 9 days across 212 agencies (internal data, Q3 2026).' Subhead: 'Get paid faster with automated invoicing.'
evals.expected_output: Uses the supplied fact. The figure 9 days comes from the context file, so no [NEED] marker asks for it and no other figure is added; a [NEED] for a different missing fact, such as a baseline for "faster", is acceptable. Returns just the changed line with a reason.
assertions: Uses the 9-day figure from the context file
Adds no figure that is not in the prompt
Does not write a [NEED] marker asking for a fact that was supplied

evals.prompt: Make this homepage hero more specific and persuasive: 'Our software helps teams finish projects faster and save money.' There is no product-marketing context file and I have no figures to give you.
evals.expected_output: Does not invent a percentage, dollar amount or timeframe. Sharpens what can be sharpened from the sentence itself and writes [NEED: ...] for the missing measured result, naming the evidence that would unlock it (what was measured, source, date).
assertions: Writes at least one [NEED: ...] marker for the missing result
Names the evidence that would unlock the claim
Contains no invented percentage, dollar amount or timeframe

evals.prompt: Review this testimonial section and improve it: 'CloudSync is great! It really helped our company. The team was very responsive and the product works well. We would recommend it to anyone looking for a solution. - John S., CEO'. That is all I have; there is no other detail about John or his company.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the testimonial as vague and does not rewrite it into a specific, quotable result. Offers questions to ask John S. and a template with [NEED: ...] placeholders, and notes that a changed quote needs his approval to publish.
assertions: Identifies the testimonial as too vague
Does not invent a result, figure, company name or new quote
Uses [NEED: ...] placeholders in any template
Suggests questions to get a better testimonial

evals.prompt: I need you to apply the 'So What' and 'Zero Risk' sweeps to this pricing page copy: 'Our Pro plan includes unlimited projects, advanced reporting, priority support, and custom integrations. Starting at $99/month.' I have not told you whether there is a trial, a guarantee or a cancellation policy.
evals.expected_output: Applies both sweeps. Identifies the missing risk reversal but does not write one: no trial length, guarantee period, refund or cancel-anytime term appears as copy. Writes [NEED: ...] for the terms and flags that any guarantee commits the business and needs the owner's approval.
assertions: Applies the So What sweep to each feature
Identifies the missing risk reversal
Writes [NEED: ...] instead of inventing trial, guarantee or cancellation terms
Flags that a guarantee needs the business owner's approval

evals.prompt: Add an annual plan price and the annual discount to this pricing blurb: 'Pro: unlimited projects, advanced reporting, priority support. $99/month.' I have not decided the annual price or the discount yet.
evals.expected_output: Does not compute or invent an annual price, a discount percentage or a savings figure. Writes [NEED: ...] for both and flags that a price is a commitment the business owner must approve.
assertions: Writes [NEED: ...] for the annual price and the discount
Invents no price, percentage or savings figure
Flags that the owner must approve the price

evals.prompt: Rewrite the support section of our site to sound confident and specific: 'We respond fast and we are always here when you need us.' No response-time data or support-hours policy exists.
evals.expected_output: Does not invent a response time, support hours or availability promise. Writes [NEED: ...] for the real response time and hours, and flags that a service-level promise commits the business and needs the owner's approval.
assertions: Writes [NEED: ...] for response time and support hours
Invents no response time, hours or 24/7 claim
Flags that a service-level promise needs the owner's approval
